$$S=C\sqcup L\sqcup I\sqcup P,$$
where  $C$  consists of selected star centres,  $L$  their leaves,  $I$  selected isolates, and  $P$  selected isolated-edge endpoints.Let  $W$  contain one chosen deletion witness  $w_\ell$  for every  $\ell\in L$ .2.1 The crucial minimality argumentThe subtle point is correctly handled: minimality must account for the newly omitted vertex  $\ell$ , not merely vertices that were already outside  $S$ .Delete a selected leaf  $\ell$ .Its centre remains active because the star has at least two leaves. No other selected vertex becomes inactive.Moreover, the newly omitted  $\ell$  is itself formed: its centre and another leaf provide the required two selected vertices.Consequently, some previously omitted vertex  $w_\ell$  must become unformed.The bipartite formation criterion is
$$x\text{ formed}

$$\boxed{
N_S(w_\ell)=\{\ell\}
\quad\text{or}\quad
N_S(w_\ell)=\{\ell,i_\ell\},
\quad i_\ell\in I.
}$$

$$|W|=|L|=e.$$
Importantly, this does not require witnesses to be independent. They may be adjacent, and a selected isolate may help arbitrarily many witnesses.2.2 Exact restricted optimizationDefine
$$Q=G[W\cup I].$$

$$D\cap C=\varnothing.$$

$$D\cap(W\cup I)$$
is independent in  $Q$ .The old selected edges  $P$  are unaffected: there are no edges from  $W$  to  $P$  or  $C$ , and the selected leaves have no additional selected neighbours outside their centres.Conversely, every independent set  $J$  of  $Q$  gives a valid dissociation set
$$D=L\cup P\cup J.$$
This proves both directions of the optimization, not just a lower bound.Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
\max_D |D|
&=|L|+|P|+\alpha(Q)\\
&=|S|-c+e-\nu(Q).
\end{aligned}$$

$$\boxed{\max_{\substack{D\subseteq S\cup W,\ L\subseteq D\\\Delta(G[D])\leq1}}|D|=|S|-c+e-\nu(Q)}$$

$$K=(A\setminus Z)\cup(B\cap Z)$$
is a vertex cover.No unmatched right vertex can be reached, since that would produce an augmenting path.Each matching edge contributes exactly one vertex to  $K$ . Thus
$$|K|=|M|=\nu(Q).$$
The complement of  $K$  is a maximum independent set.The resulting exchange is explicitly
$$D=((S\setminus C)\cup W)\setminus K.$$
Its size is
$$|D|=|S|-c+e-|K|.$$
The construction counts a shared helper isolate only once. No vertex is allocated twice.Conclusion: the exact matching formula and its constructive certificates are established.3. Consequences and integer thresholdsThe no-isolate consequence is correct.If no selected isolate is touched, then
$$\nu(Q)\leq\left\lfloor\frac e2\right\rfloor.$$

$$e\geq2c.$$
Therefore
$$e-\nu(Q)
\geq \left\lceil\frac e2\right\rceil
\geq c.$$
It follows that
$$|S|\leq\beta_2(G).$$

$$K_A=W_B\cup J_B,\qquad
K_B=W_A\cup J_A$$
are valid, including when untouched isolates are present.They give
$$\beta_2(G)
\geq |S|-c+\max(e_A-t_B,e_B-t_A).$$

$$\boxed{
\beta_2(G)\geq

Thus the sufficient threshold is
$$\boxed{e-t\geq2c-1.}$$
The minus-one is correct. Replacing it with  $2c$  would unnecessarily weaken the result.For a genuine deficit  $d=|S|-\beta_2(G)>0$ , the inequality implies
